value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 本紀第一 太祖一
value.en: Annals 1: Taizu, Part One
value.literal: Annals 1, Taizu 1

value.zh: 冬十月甲辰，遣起居注吳琳、魏觀以幣求遺賢於四方。
value.en: On jiachen day in the tenth month of winter he sent imperial diarists Wu Lin and Wei Guan with gifts to seek worthy men in every quarter.
value.literal: On day jiachen in the tenth month of winter he sent imperial diarists Wu Lin and Wei Guan with gifts to seek worthy men throughout the realm.

value.zh: 丙午，令百官禮儀尚左。
value.en: On bingwu day he ordered that official ceremony honor the left.
value.literal: On day bingwu he ordered that ceremonial precedence in the bureaucracy honor the left.

value.zh: 改李善長左相國，徐達右相國。
value.en: Li Shanchang was made left chief councillor and Xu Da right chief councillor.
value.literal: Li Shanchang was made left chief councillor, Xu Da right chief councillor.

value.zh: 辛亥，祀元臣余闕於安慶，李黼於江州。
value.en: On xinhai day he offered sacrifice to the Yuan loyalists Yu Que at Anqing and Li Fu at Jiangzhou.
value.literal: On day xinhai he sacrificed to the Yuan loyalists Yu Que at Anqing and Li Fu at Jiangzhou.

value.zh: 壬子，置御史臺。
value.en: On renzi day the Censorate was established.
value.literal: On day renzi the Censorate was established.

value.zh: 癸丑，湯和為征南將軍，吳禎副之，討國珍。
value.en: On guichou day Tang He was made grand general for the southern expedition and Wu Zhen his deputy, to campaign against Guozhen.
value.literal: On day guichou Tang He was made grand general for the southern expedition and Wu Zhen his deputy, to attack Guozhen.

value.zh: 甲寅，定律令。
value.en: On jiayin day laws and ordinances were promulgated.
value.literal: On day jiayin laws and ordinances were promulgated.

value.zh: 戊午，正郊社、太廟雅樂。
value.en: On wuwu day the ceremonial music of the suburban altars and Imperial Temple was set right.
value.literal: On day wuwu the ritual music of the suburban altars and Imperial Temple was corrected.

value.zh: 陶安，字主敬，當塗人。
value.en: Tao An, styled Zhujing, was from Dangtu.
value.literal: Tao An, with the style name Zhujing, was a man of Dangtu.

value.zh: 少敏悟，博涉經史，尤長於《易》。
value.en: As a youth he was exceptionally quick-witted; he read widely in the classics and histories and was especially skilled in the Book of Changes.
value.literal: In youth he was perceptive and quick; he ranged broadly through the classics and histories, and was especially accomplished in the Book of Changes.

value.zh: 元至正初，舉江浙鄉試，授明道書院山長，避亂家居。
value.en: Early in the Zhizheng reign, he passed the Jiang and Zhe regional examination and was appointed director of the Mingdao Academy; he then retired at home to escape the civil unrest.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan Zhizheng era, he passed the Jiang-Zhe provincial examination, was appointed headmaster of the Mingdao Academy, and stayed at home to avoid the turmoil.

value.zh: 太祖取太平，安與耆儒李習率父老出迎。
value.en: When the founding emperor captured Taiping, An and the elder scholar Li Xi led the local elders out to welcome him.
value.literal: When the Taizu emperor took Taiping, An together with the venerable scholar Li Xi led the elders to go out and welcome him.

value.zh: 太祖召與語。
value.en: The emperor summoned him for an audience.
value.literal: The Taizu emperor summoned him and conversed with him.

value.zh: 安進曰：「海內鼎沸，豪傑並爭，然其意在子女玉帛，非有撥亂、救民、安天下心。
value.en: An spoke up: "The empire is in uproar and rival strongmen fight one another, but their aim is spoil and luxury, not to restore order, relieve the people, or bring peace to the realm.
value.literal: An advanced and said: "Within the seas the tripod boils; heroes struggle with one another, yet their intent lies in children, women, jade, and silks—they lack the mind to put chaos in order, save the people, and settle all under Heaven.

value.zh: 明公渡江，神武不殺，人心悅服，應天順人。
value.en: Your Grace has crossed the Yangzi with a martial spirit that shuns needless slaughter; the people gladly submit. You answer Heaven's mandate and win men over.
value.literal: My lord has crossed the Yangzi: divine in martial prowess and sparing in killing; hearts rejoice and submit—he responds to Heaven and accords with men.

value.zh: 以行吊伐，天下不足平也。」
value.en: March forth as the champion of the wronged, and pacifying the realm will be a small matter."
value.literal: By acting as one who comforts the wronged and punishes the guilty, all under Heaven is not enough to remain un pacified."

value.zh: 太祖問曰：「吾欲取金陵，何如？」
value.en: The emperor asked, "I mean to take Jinling. What do you think?"
value.literal: The Taizu emperor asked: "I wish to take Jinling—how would that be?"

value.zh: 安曰：「金陵，古帝王都。
value.en: An replied, "Jinling was the seat of emperors in antiquity.
value.literal: An said: "Jinling is the ancient capital of emperors and kings.

value.zh: 取而有之，撫形勝以臨四方，何向不克？」
value.en: Seize it and hold its strategic heights to command the four quarters—what enemy could withstand you?"
value.literal: Take it and possess it; soothe its commanding terrain to look down on the four directions—what direction would not be overcome?"

value.zh: 太祖曰：「善。」
value.en: The emperor said, "Well said."
value.literal: The Taizu emperor said: "Good."

value.zh: 留參幕府，授左司員外郎，以習為太平知府。
value.en: He was retained on the military staff as Left Department Assistant Director, and Li Xi was appointed prefect of Taiping.
value.literal: He was kept to participate in the staff headquarters and appointed Left Department Assistant Director; Li Xi was made Taiping prefect.

value.zh: 習字伯羽，年八十余矣，卒於官。
value.en: Li Xi, styled Boyu, was over eighty and died in his post.
value.literal: Xi, style name Boyu, was more than eighty years old and died in office.

value.zh: 洪武元年，與侍御史文原吉、起居注魏觀等循行天下，訪求賢才。
value.en: In the first Hongwu year he traveled the realm with the attending censor Wen Yuanji, the recorder Wei Guan, and others to seek out men of talent.
value.literal: In Hongwu year one, together with Attending Censor Wen Yuanji, Daily Records Wei Guan, and others, he made a circuit of all under Heaven seeking worthy talents.

value.zh: 還，進翰林直學士，遷侍讀學士。
value.en: On his return he was made a direct Hanlin academician and then promoted to reader-in-waiting.
value.literal: On return he advanced to Hanlin Direct Academician and was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting.

value.zh: 帝御下峻，御史中丞劉基曰：「古者公卿有罪，盤水加劍，詣請室自裁，所以勵廉恥，存國體也。」
value.en: The emperor ruled harshly. Vice censor-in-chief Liu Ji said, "In antiquity, when high ministers offended, they were given a tray of water and a sword and went to the execution chamber to take their own lives—this was how integrity was enforced and the dignity of the state preserved."
value.literal: The emperor was stern toward subordinates; Vice Censor-in-chief Liu Ji said: "In antiquity when dukes and ministers had offenses, tray of water and sword were added; they went to the execution chamber to cut themselves short—this was to encourage integrity and shame and preserve the state's stature."

value.zh: 同時侍側，遂取《戴記》及賈誼疏以進，復剴切言之。
value.en: Tong, who was attending nearby, cited the Record of Rites and Jia Yi's memorial and pressed the point with further earnest argument.
value.literal: Tong was at the time attending at his side; he thereupon took the Record of Rites and Jia Yi's memorial and advanced them, again speaking with earnest incisiveness.

value.zh: 帝嘗與侍臣言：聲色之害甚於鴆毒，創業之君，為子孫所承式，尤不可不謹。
value.en: The emperor once told his attendants that the lure of pleasure was deadlier than poison and that a founding ruler, being the model for his heirs, must be doubly careful.
value.literal: The emperor once spoke to attendant ministers: the harm of sound and color exceeds that of poison wine; a ruler who founds the enterprise is the model his descendants inherit—especially he must be cautious.

value.zh: 同因舉成湯不邇聲色，垂裕後昆以對。
value.en: Tong answered by citing how King Tang kept his distance from sensual delights to leave a legacy for his descendants.
value.literal: Tong thereupon cited that King Tang did not approach sound and color, extending abundance to his posterity, in reply.

value.zh: 其因事納忠如此。
value.en: Thus he offered loyal remonstrance whenever occasion arose.
value.literal: His offering loyal counsel on occasions was like this.

value.zh: 贊曰：明初之議禮也，宋濂方家居，諸儀率多陶安裁定。
value.en: The appraiser writes: When the Ming first debated ritual, Song Lian was still in retirement and Tao An settled most of the forms.
value.literal: The eulogy says: In the early Ming deliberation on ritual, Song Lian was still at home; the various ceremonies were mostly drawn up and settled by Tao An.

value.zh: 大祀禮專用安議，其餘參匯諸說，從其所長：祫禘用詹同，時享用硃升，釋奠、耕耤用錢用壬，五祀用崔亮，朝會用劉基，祝祭用魏觀，軍禮用陶凱。
value.en: Great sacrifices followed An exclusively; other rites combined specialists—Zhan Tong for collective and seasonal rites, Zhu Sheng for seasonal offerings, Qian Yongren for Confucian sacrifice and plowing, Cui Liang for the five sacrifices, Liu Ji for court audiences, Wei Guan for prayer sacrifices, and Tao Kai for military ritual.
value.literal: Great-sacrifice ritual exclusively used An's deliberations; the rest combined various opinions, following each man's strength: collective and seasonal sacrifice used Zhan Tong, seasonal offerings used Zhu Sheng, Confucian sacrifice and royal plowing used Qian Yongren, the five sacrifices used Cui Liang, court audiences used Liu Ji, prayer-sacrifice used Wei Guan, military ritual used Tao Kai.

value.zh: 皆能援據經義，酌古準今，郁然成一代休明之治。
value.en: All cited the classics, weighed antiquity against the present, and helped shape a brilliant age of governance.
value.literal: All were able to cite classical meaning, weigh antiquity against the present, and richly form the brilliant governance of a generation.

value.zh: 雖折中斷制，裁自上心，諸臣之功亦曷可少哉。
value.en: Though final decisions rested with the emperor, the ministers' contributions can hardly be slighted.
value.literal: Although the final compromise and judgment and cutting were from the ruler's own mind, how could the merit of the various ministers be slighted?

value.literal: (Sun Rujing)〉

value.zh: 明開國時即重師儒官。
value.en: From the founding of the dynasty, Ming already placed great weight on posts for teachers and Confucian scholars.
value.literal: At the founding of Ming, posts for masters and Confucian scholars were already highly valued.

value.zh: 許存仁、魏觀為祭酒，老成端謹；
value.en: Xu Cunren and Wei Guan served as Chancellor; they were mature, steady, and dignified;
value.literal: Xu Cunren and Wei Guan served as Chancellor; they were mature, steady, and careful;

value.zh: 訥稍晚進，最蒙遇。
value.en: Ne entered somewhat later and enjoyed the greatest imperial favor.
value.literal: Ne entered somewhat later and received the greatest favor.

value.zh: 與訥定學規者，司業王嘉會、龔斅。
value.en: Those who worked with Ne to establish the school regulations were Vice Chancellors Wang Jiahui and Gong Xiao.
value.literal: Those who with Ne established the school regulations were Vice Chancellors Wang Jiahui and Gong Xiao.

value.zh: 三人年俱高，鬚髮皓白，終日危坐，堂上肅然。
value.en: All three were advanced in years, with snow-white beards and hair; they sat upright throughout the day, and the hall was solemn.
value.literal: All three were advanced in years, their beards and hair snow-white; they sat upright all day, and the hall was solemn.

value.zh: 而張美和、聶鉉、貝瓊等皆名儒，當洪武時，先後為博士、助教、學錄，以故諸生多所成就。
value.en: Zhang Meihe, Nie Xuan, Bei Qiong, and others were all renowned Confucian scholars; during Hongwu they served in turn as Erudite, Assistant Instructor, and Recorder, and for this reason many students achieved distinction.
value.literal: Moreover Zhang Meihe, Nie Xuan, Bei Qiong, and others were all famous Confucians; during Hongwu they served in succession as Erudite, Assistant Instructor, and Recorder, and for this reason many students achieved distinction.

value.zh: 魏觀事別載。
value.en: Wei Guan's biography is recorded separately.
value.literal: Wei Guan's affairs are recorded separately.

value.en: Xie Duo and Lu Duo

value.literal: (Zhao Yong)〉

value.zh: 贊曰：明太祖時，國學師儒，體貌優重。
value.en: The historian comments: Under the founding emperor, Imperial University teachers enjoyed exceptional honor.
value.literal: The comment says: In the time of Ming Taizu, teachers at the Imperial Academy received preferential treatment in bearing and status.

value.zh: 魏觀、宋訥為祭酒，造就人才，克舉其職。
value.en: As chancellors, Wei Guan and Song Na trained talent and fulfilled their roles.
value.literal: Wei Guan and Song Na as chancellors molded talent and fully performed their duties.

value.zh: 諸生銜命奉使，往往擢為大官，不專以科目進也。
value.en: Students sent on missions often rose to high office without relying solely on examinations.
value.literal: Students bearing orders on missions were often promoted to high office; advancement was not solely through the examination track.

value.zh: 中葉以還，流品稍雜，撥歷亦為具文，成均師席，不過為儒臣序遷之地而已。
value.en: By mid-dynasty ranks grew mixed and practical training became nominal; the chancellorship was merely another step for literati.
value.literal: From the mid-dynasty onward the stream of ranks grew somewhat mixed; practical assignments also became empty form; the master's seat at the Imperial Academy was no more than a place in the orderly promotion of scholar-officials.

value.zh: 李時勉、陳敬宗諸人，方廉清鯁，表範卓然，類而傳之，庶觀者有所法焉。
value.en: Yet Li Shimian, Chen Jingzong, and their peers were upright exemplars; recorded together, they might still teach later ages.
value.literal: Li Shimian, Chen Jingzong, and the others were upright, pure, and stern, with outstanding models; if grouped and transmitted, perhaps observers would have something to emulate.

value.zh: 撫水州 廣源州 黎洞 環州
value.en: Fu Shuizhou, Guang Yuanzhou, the Li Dong, and Huan Zhou.
value.literal: Fu Shuizhou, Guang Yuanzhou, Li Dong, and Huan Zhou.

value.zh: 是時，天下久安，嶺南州縣無備，一旦兵起倉卒，不知所為，守將多棄城遁。
value.en: The empire had been at peace for years, and Lingnan had no defenses. When rebellion erupted overnight, local commanders panicked and many fled their posts.
value.literal: At this time, the realm had long been at peace; Lingnan prefectures and counties had no preparedness. Suddenly troops rose in haste, not knowing what to do—the defending generals mostly abandoned cities and fled.

value.zh: 故智高所向得志，相繼破橫、貴、龔、潯、藤、梧、封、康、端九州，害曹覲於封州、趙師旦馬貴於康州，餘殺官吏甚眾。
value.en: Zhigao swept through Heng, Gui, Gong, Xun, Teng, Wu, Feng, Kang, and Duan, killing Cao Jin at Fengzhou and Zhao Shidan and Ma Gui at Kangzhou along with countless other officials.
value.literal: Therefore wherever Zhigao went he got his wish; in succession he broke the nine prefectures of Heng, Gui, Gong, Xun, Teng, Wu, Feng, Kang, and Duan, killed Cao Jin at Feng Prefecture and Zhao Shidan and Ma Gui at Kang Prefecture; besides these he killed very many officials.

value.zh: 所過焚府庫，進圍廣州。
value.en: His army burned treasuries along the way and pushed on to besiege Guangzhou.
value.literal: Where he passed he burned government storehouses, advancing to besiege Guangzhou.

value.zh: 初，智高將至，守將仲簡不許民入保城中，民不得入者皆附智高，智高勢益張。
value.en: When Zhigao approached, Defender Zhong Jian refused to let civilians into the city. Those left outside joined the rebels, and Zhigao's forces swelled.
value.literal: Initially, as Zhigao was about to arrive, the defending general Zhong Jian did not permit the people to enter and take refuge within the city; those who could not enter all attached to Zhigao, and Zhigao's power grew ever greater.

value.zh: 先是，魏瓘築州城，鑿井畜水，作大弩為守備。
value.en: Earlier, Wei Guan had fortified the city with walls, wells, and giant crossbows.
value.literal: Earlier, Wei Guan had built the prefectural city wall, dug wells to store water, and made large crossbows for defensive preparation.

value.zh: 至是，智高為雲梯土山，攻城甚急，又斷流水，而城堅，井飲不竭，弩發，中輒洞潰，智高力屈。
value.en: Zhigao built siege towers and ramparts and cut off the water supply, but the walls held, the wells never ran dry, and Wei Guan's crossbows punched clean holes through his ranks until Zhigao's army was spent.
value.literal: At this time, Zhigao made cloud-ladders and earthen mounds, attacking the city very urgently; he also cut off the flowing water, but the walls were strong, well water for drinking did not run dry, crossbows fired, and hits immediately pierced through and burst; Zhigao's strength was exhausted.

value.zh: 會知英州蘇緘屯兵邊渡村，扼其歸路；
value.en: Meanwhile Yingzhou Prefect Su Jian blocked the retreat at Biandu Village;
value.literal: It happened that Ying Prefecture prefect Su Jian stationed troops at Biandu Village, blocking his route of return;

value.zh: 番禺縣令蕭注募土丁及海上強壯二千餘人，與智高眾格鬥，焚其戰艦；
value.en: Panyu Magistrate Xiao Zhu rallied over two thousand local militiamen and sailors, fought Zhigao's troops, and burned his fleet;
value.literal: Panyu county magistrate Xiao Zhu recruited more than two thousand local militia and strong men from the sea, grappled with Zhigao's masses, and burned his warships;

value.zh: 轉運使王罕亦自外至，益修守備。
value.en: Transport Commissioner Wang Han arrived from outside and tightened the defenses.
value.literal: Transport commissioner Wang Han also arrived from outside, further repairing defensive preparations.

value.zh: 智高知不可拔，圍五十七日，七月壬戌，解去。
value.en: After fifty-seven days, seeing Guangzhou could not be taken, Zhigao withdrew on the renxu day of the seventh month.
value.literal: Zhigao knew it could not be taken; he besieged for fifty-seven days; on the renxu day of the seventh month, he lifted the siege and departed.

value.zh: 由清遠濟江，擁婦女作樂而行，遇張忠戰於白田，忠死之。
value.en: He crossed the river near Qingyuan, marching to music with captive women until Zhang Zhong intercepted him at Baitian and was killed.
value.literal: By Qingyuan he crossed the river, embracing women and making music as he went; he encountered Zhang Zhong and fought at Baitian; Zhong died in it.

value.zh: 去攻賀州，不克，夜害蔣偕於太平場。
value.en: Failing to take Hezhou, he ambushed and killed Jiang Xie at Taiping that night.
value.literal: He went on to attack He Prefecture, did not overcome it; at night he harmed Jiang Xie at Taiping Ground.

value.zh: 九月庚申，破昭州，害王正倫等於館門驛。
value.en: On the gengshen day of the ninth month he seized Zhaozhou and murdered Wang Zhenglun and others at Guanmen Post Station.
value.literal: On the gengshen day of the ninth month, he broke Zhao Prefecture, harming Wang Zhenglun and others at Guanmen Post Station.

value.zh: 州之山有數穴，大可容數百千人，民聞兵至，走匿其中，智高知之，縱火，皆焚死。
value.en: Locals fled into mountain caves that could shelter thousands. Zhigao found them and set the caves ablaze, burning everyone inside.
value.literal: The prefecture's mountains had several caves, large enough to hold several hundred or thousand people; when the people heard troops arrive, they ran and hid within them; Zhigao knew this, set fire, and all were burned to death.

value.zh: 十月丁丑，破賓州。
value.en: On the dingchou day of the tenth month he captured Binzhou.
value.literal: On the dingchou day of the tenth month, he broke Bin Prefecture.

value.zh: 甲申，復據邕州，日夜伐木治舟楫，揚言復趨廣州。
value.en: On the jiashen day he retook Yongzhou, cutting timber day and night to build boats while boasting he would strike Guangzhou again.
value.literal: On the jiashen day, he again occupied Yong Prefecture, day and night felling trees to build boats and oars, proclaiming he would again rush toward Guangzhou.

value.zh: 十二月壬申，又敗陳曙於金城驛。
value.en: On the renshen day of the twelfth month he routed Chen Shu at Jincheng Post Station.
value.literal: On the renshen day of the twelfth month, he again defeated Chen Shu at Jincheng Post Station.

value.zh: 初，智高以反聞，朝廷命曙就擊之，既而楊畋、曹修、張忠、蔣偕相繼出，又以余靖、孫沔為安撫使。
value.en: Zhigao's disinformation first drew Chen Shu, then Yang Tian, Cao Xiu, Zhang Zhong, and Jiang Xie; the court also appointed Yu Jing and Sun Mian as pacification commissioners.
value.literal: Initially, Zhigao by false intelligence misled the court to order Shu to go and strike him; afterward Yang Tian, Cao Xiu, Zhang Zhong, and Jiang Xie successively went out; again Yu Jing and Sun Mian were made pacification commissioners.

value.zh: 畋、修聞智高至，退軍避之。
value.en: Yang Tian and Cao Xiu retreated as soon as they heard Zhigao was near.
value.literal: Tian and Xiu, hearing Zhigao had arrived, withdrew their armies to avoid him.

value.zh: 忠、偕勇而無謀，皆死。
value.en: Zhang Zhong and Jiang Xie fought boldly but recklessly, and both were killed.
value.literal: Zhong and Xie were brave but without strategy; both died.

value.zh: 智高益自恣，南土騷然。
value.en: Zhigao grew bolder still, and the south was in turmoil.
value.literal: Zhigao grew ever more self-indulgent; the southern lands were in uproar.

value.zh: 仁宗以為憂，命狄青為宣撫使，諸將皆受青節制。
value.en: Alarmed, Emperor Renzong put Di Qing in overall command, with every general under his authority.
value.literal: Emperor Renzong regarded it as a worry, and ordered Di Qing as pacification commissioner; all generals were under Qing's command and control.

value.zh: 曙恐青至有功，亟挑戰，故敗。
value.en: Chen Shu, afraid Di Qing would win the glory, rashly offered battle and was defeated.
value.literal: Shu feared that when Qing arrived there would be merit, and urgently challenged battle; therefore he was defeated.

value.zh: 韋孝寬 韋敻 梁士彥
value.en: Biographies of Wei Xiaokuan, Wei Xiong, and Liang Shiyan
value.literal: Wei Xiaokuan; Wei Xiong; Liang Shiyan

value.zh: 敻子瓘行隨州刺史，因疾物故，孝寬子總復於并州戰歿。
value.en: Wei Xiong's son Guan, acting governor of Sui, died of illness, and Wei Xiaokuan's son Zong was killed in battle at Bing.
value.literal: Xiong's son Guan was acting governor of Sui Prefecture and died of illness; Xiaokuan's son Zong also fell in battle at Bing Prefecture.

value.zh: 一日之中，凶問俱至。
value.en: Within a single day news of both deaths arrived.
value.literal: Within a single day, tidings of both deaths arrived.

value.zh: 家人相對悲慟，而敻神色自若。
value.en: The household wept together, but Wei Xiong's face stayed unchanged.
value.literal: The household faced one another in grief and lamentation, yet Xiong's expression remained as usual.

value.zh: 謂之曰：「死生命也，去來常事，亦何足悲。」
value.en: He told them, "Life and death are fate; coming and going are ordinary things—what is there to mourn?"
value.literal: He said to them: "Life and death are fate; coming and going are ordinary affairs—what is there worth grieving over?"

value.zh: 援琴撫之如舊。
value.en: He took up his zither and played as before.
value.literal: He took up the zither and played it as before.
